documents.name: MiniCPM-OCR 1.0
documents.description: Set up MiniCPM-OCR 1.0's SDK and recognition service, check layout dependencies and verify Markdown, tables and document results before downstream automation.
documents.introduction:
## What is MiniCPM-OCR 1.0?

[MiniCPM-OCR 1.0](https://huggingface.co/openbmb/MiniCPM-OCR-1.0) is OpenBMB's 1.3B-parameter model for document recognition. The official project describes support for Chinese and English text, tables, formulas, charts, seals and structured information extraction.

A practical use is converting a scanned document or PDF into Markdown and structured JSON for review or downstream processing. Recognition output still needs checking against the original document, especially for numbers, reading order and table structure.

This guide follows the [official repository](https://github.com/OpenBMB/MiniCPM-OCR) and deployment tutorial checked November 2, 2026. It does not report a local inference test or an independent benchmark.

## Understand the two-part runtime

The documented local deployment separates two jobs:

- The SDK detects layout, crops regions and assembles results.
- The inference service runs the recognition model.

The tutorial uses separate Python environments and terminals for these parts. Installing the SDK alone does not start the recognition service.

The default accelerated path also uses DSpark speculative decoding, which needs a main model and a compatible draft model from the same release. A draft model is an additional inference component, not a replacement for the main OCR checkpoint.

The layout detector is another dependency: PP-DocLayoutV3. Check that its model files are available before treating an incomplete setup as an OCR failure.

## Choose a deployment route before installing

The official Linux vLLM tutorial specifies a Linux x86_64 environment, an NVIDIA GPU, a driver requirement and substantial disk space for environments, source builds, models and caches. It reports verification on an RTX 5090 with 32 GB memory; that is not a universal minimum-hardware guarantee.

Read the [current requirements](https://github.com/OpenBMB/MiniCPM-OCR/blob/main/docs/minicpm_ocr_tutorial_en.md) against your actual machine. Building an inference framework and loading a model are different resource demands.

The repository also links SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama and FlagOS guides. Follow one backend's instructions and use its matching checkpoint format. Do not mix a GGUF checkpoint with a startup command written for the original vLLM model.

For a first evaluation without building the runtime, the model card links official online demonstrations. A hosted demonstration and a fully local deployment have different data paths and operating limits.

## Connect the SDK to a running service

The vLLM tutorial starts the recognition service on loopback port 18499 with the served model name `minicpm-ocr`. After following that service setup, its SDK example is:

```bash
minicpmvocr parse \
  --device cuda:0 \
  --server-url http://127.0.0.1:18499 \
  --model minicpm-ocr \
  --input doc.pdf \
  --output doc.md
```

This command assumes the documented SDK environment, a working GPU layout detector and the matching recognition service. Replace the input and output paths with your own sample paths.

Check the service's `/v1/models` response before sending a document. Confirm the endpoint, port and served model name rather than copying a name from a different backend.

Some quick-start examples elsewhere use port 8080. Either can be a valid configured endpoint; what matters is that the SDK points to the service you actually started.

## Verify the result, not just the process

Start with a short document whose correct contents you can inspect. Keep the original alongside the output and check:

1. Every expected page appears, in order.
2. Paragraphs follow the intended reading sequence.
3. Table rows, columns and merged cells remain understandable.
4. Formulas preserve their symbols and structure.
5. Dates, identifiers, amounts and units match the source.
6. Output paths contain the expected Markdown and structured results.

The project represents tables as HTML and formulas as LaTeX in its parsing workflow. Inspect those structures rather than judging only a rendered preview.

A successful process exit or an HTTP response proves that part of the pipeline ran. It does not prove that every value was recognized correctly. For downstream automation, define what counts as a missing field and keep source references so discrepancies can be reviewed.

## Recognition and quality scoring are separate

The same repository includes MiniCPM-OCR Jev, a separate model that scores an image together with an OCR result. MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 performs recognition; adding a quality scorer is an additional workflow decision.

A score is a signal for selecting content to review. It does not independently certify a document, and a threshold should be checked on samples from the real application.

The maintainers publish benchmark and throughput figures with specific test configurations. Treat those as upstream results. Your document mix, hardware, backend and concurrency can produce different behavior.

## Local processing, downloads and costs

The deployment tutorial states that the local SDK and recognition service can process documents without a cloud OCR service. Initial dependency and model downloads still require network access.

Keep the configured endpoint in view: using a remote recognition service changes where document data is processed. Do not assume an SDK invocation is local simply because its command runs on your laptop.

The model card identifies an Apache-2.0 license. Hardware, hosting and any third-party service can have separate costs. The repository links a “Free API,” but this guide does not promise a particular quota or indefinite free access.

For preparing input files, see [Filee](https://findryai.com/item/filee). Browse [Developer Tools](https://findryai.com/category/developer-tools) for related document-processing utilities.

## Official sources

- [MiniCPM-OCR repository: runtime components and model roles](https://github.com/OpenBMB/MiniCPM-OCR)
- [Local installation and inference tutorial](https://github.com/OpenBMB/MiniCPM-OCR/blob/main/docs/minicpm_ocr_tutorial_en.md)
- [Official MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 model card](https://huggingface.co/openbmb/MiniCPM-OCR-1.0)

Sources checked November 2, 2026. No local deployment, recognition-quality test or speed measurement was performed for this listing.
